justification: The repository exhibits high coupling and poor cohesion in configuration and service layers. The AppConfig class in app/config.py directly handles file I/O, password encryption, and business logic (e.g., _auto_encrypt_password, set_password, mark_initialized) in a single monolithic module. This forces changes to any aspect of configuration to touch the same file, increasing risk and complexity. Similarly, service modules like app/services/admin_agent_query_service.py and app/services/admin_task_query_service.py contain both query construction and serialization logic in tightly coupled methods, making it difficult to modify one concern without affecting the other. Localized Modification will increase cohesion by grouping related responsibilities into smaller, focused modules, reducing the scope of change and improving maintainability.
expected_architectural_change: The AppConfig class will be decomposed into dedicated modules: ConfigLoader (file I/O), PasswordManager (bcrypt operations), and ConfigValidator (business rules). Similarly, query services will be split into QueryBuilder (SQL construction), Serializer (data transformation), and Validator (input validation) modules. This creates smaller, single-responsibility modules where changes are localized and less likely to ripple across the codebase.
implementation_strategy: 1. Extract password handling from AppConfig into app/services/password_manager.py with methods like hash_password and verify_password. 2. Extract YAML loading/saving into app/services/config_loader.py. 3. Refactor AppConfig to delegate to these new modules. 4. In admin_agent_query_service.py, extract subqueries (e.g., _build_agent_workload_stats_subquery) into app/services/agent_workload_stats.py. 5. Extract serialization logic (_serialize_agent_list_row) into app/services/agent_serializer.py. 6. Repeat for admin_task_query_service.py and admin_score_query_service.py. 7. Update imports and routing to use new modules. This can be done incrementally, one service at a time, without disrupting existing functionality.
risks: Risk of temporary duplication during refactoring (e.g., old and new modules coexisting). Mitigation: Use feature flags or conditional imports to gradually migrate. Risk of increased import complexity if modules are over-partitioned. Mitigation: Keep module boundaries aligned with business capabilities (e.g., 'password' and 'config' stay together; 'query' and 'serialization' split). Risk of performance overhead from extra function calls. Mitigation: Profile after refactoring; inline hot paths if needed.
